workflow.purpose:
Create or update a pattern document in `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem-name]/patterns/`.
A pattern doc describes a reusable structural approach used by 2+ implementations. It is the document an AI agent reads to ensure new code follows established conventions — structure diagram, how it works, how to apply, current implementations.
This workflow is executed directly — NO sub-agents are spawned. The executing agent does everything: finding implementations, extracting the abstract pattern, and writing the document.
workflow.mandatory-context: Read all files referenced by the invoking command's execution-context before starting. Also read any document or text passed as parameter ($ARGUMENTS) in the invoking command.

process.step:
Display stage banner:
``` ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ACE > Map Pattern ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ```
Parse $ARGUMENTS for: `text`, `subsystem`, `story-context`, `commits`.
**If `text` is missing:** Ask the user: - header: "Pattern" - question: "Describe the pattern to document — what structural approach is reused?\nE.g., 'Template Method pattern used by all drawing paths'"
**If `subsystem` is missing:** Ask the user: - header: "Pattern" - question: "Which subsystem does this pattern belong to?"
Resolve the subsystem. Check if `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem-name]/` exists.
**If not found:** ``` ! No wiki found for subsystem "[subsystem]". Run /ace:map-subsystem first to create the subsystem wiki. ``` Exit.
Ensure patterns directory exists: ```bash mkdir -p .docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/patterns ```
Display: ``` i Pattern: [text description] Subsystem: [subsystem-name] Story context: [path/issue, or "none"] Commits: [value, or "search codebase directly"] ```
Continue to step 2.

Scan for existing pattern docs:
``` Glob(pattern='*.md', path='.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/patterns') ```
**If existing pattern docs found:** Read their titles and "The Pattern" sections. Check if any covers the same or overlapping structural approach.
**If overlap detected:** Use AskUserQuestion: - header: "Pattern" - question: "An existing pattern doc may cover a similar approach:\n\n- `[existing-file]`: [title]\n\nShould I update the existing doc or create a new one?" - options: - "Update existing" — set MODE = update, set TARGET_FILE = existing path - "Create new" — set MODE = create
**If no overlap or no existing pattern docs:** Set MODE = create.
**If MODE = create:** Derive file name from pattern name in kebab-case. Set TARGET_FILE = `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/patterns/[pattern-name].md`
Continue to step 3.

Read all markdown files in the story artifacts folder. Extract: what pattern was used, what was implemented.
```bash gh issue view [issue-number] --json title,body,labels,comments ``` Extract context about the pattern.
Skip — discover pattern from codebase only.
```bash git diff --name-only HEAD~[N]..HEAD ``` Start with changed files. Read them to identify the pattern. Then search the full codebase for other implementations of the same pattern.
```bash git diff --name-only [first-sha]^..[last-sha] ``` Start with changed files. Read them to identify the pattern. Then search the full codebase for other implementations.
Use the `text` description to find the pattern and its implementations:
1. Read the subsystem's structure.md and architecture.md for orientation 2. Grep for keywords from the text description (base classes, interfaces, etc.) 3. Find the abstract base/interface that defines the pattern 4. Find ALL concrete implementations (use Grep for extends/implements) 5. Read each implementation to understand the pattern mechanics
**A pattern requires 2+ implementations.** If only 1 found, ask the user: - header: "Pattern" - question: "I found only 1 implementation of this pattern. Patterns typically need 2+. Should I continue documenting it as a pattern, or is there another implementation I'm missing?"
From the implementations, extract the abstract pattern:
1. What is the base class / interface contract? 2. What factory methods / abstract methods must be overridden? 3. What is the template method / orchestration flow? 4. What are the extension points? 5. What registrations/configurations are required? 6. What are the common gotchas across implementations?
Build a complete mental model of the pattern.
Continue to step 4.

Read ALL existing wiki docs under `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/` for cross-referencing.
Follow the pattern template structure exactly.
- Title: "# [Pattern Name]" - The Pattern: ONE paragraph — what it is, when to use it. Name the GoF/industry pattern if applicable, then explain how it manifests in THIS codebase. Not a textbook definition.
Build a mermaid classDiagram showing the pattern's structure. Show the abstract/interface hierarchy with key method signatures. Show the pattern skeleton — not every concrete implementation.
Numbered steps tracing the pattern's execution flow. Every step references actual code with `file:ClassName.method`. Focus on mechanics an agent needs to understand.
The MOST ACTIONABLE section. Steps for creating a new instance: - Which files to create - Which registrations to add - Which factories to update - Reference existing implementations as "copy from" targets
Complete list of ALL known implementations with file paths. Agent uses this as a reference gallery.
Timing issues, naming conventions, registration requirements, common mistakes. Anything an agent would get wrong on first attempt.
**If MODE = create:** Write the complete document to TARGET_FILE. **If MODE = update:** Read the existing doc, add new implementations, update How to Apply if changed, add new gotchas. Write to TARGET_FILE.
Continue to step 5.

Re-read TARGET_FILE and verify:
50+ lines of substantial content "The Pattern" section present (ONE paragraph, codebase-specific) Mermaid classDiagram present showing pattern structure "How It Works" has numbered steps with code references "How to Apply" is actionable with concrete steps and "copy from" targets "Current Implementations" lists ALL known implementations with file paths At least 2 implementations listed (pattern requires 2+) "Gotchas" section present Code references use `file:Symbol` format, not line numbers No textbook definitions — pattern is codebase-specific No filler phrases, no generic advice
Fix any failures by editing the document directly.
``` Grep( pattern="(sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}|sk_live_|sk_test_|ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}|AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}|-----BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY)", path="[TARGET_FILE]", output_mode="content" ) ```
SECRETS_FOUND — alert user, do NOT commit. CLEAN.
```bash git add [TARGET_FILE] git commit -m "docs([subsystem_name]): add pattern — [pattern-name]" ```
Display:
``` ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ACE > Map Pattern > Complete ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
+ [TARGET_FILE] ([line count] lines)
Pattern: [text description] Implementations found: [count] Gotchas: [count]
Next > /clear first for a fresh context window, then:
/ace:map-pattern — create another pattern document /ace:map-guide — create a guide that uses this pattern /ace:map-sys-doc — document a system that uses this pattern Review file at [TARGET_FILE] ```
End workflow.

success_criteria.criterion: Pattern description parsed and subsystem validated
All implementations discovered (from commits or codebase search)
Existing pattern docs checked to avoid duplication (create vs update)
Pattern doc follows template structure from pattern.xml
Mermaid classDiagram present showing pattern structure
"How to Apply" is actionable with concrete steps and "copy from" targets
All current implementations listed with file paths
Gotchas section present with practical warnings
Code references use file:Symbol format, no line numbers
No textbook definitions — pattern is codebase-specific
No filler, no generic advice, no pseudocode
